summary: The SUB hover named the nearest substation when the mapped layer had a name for it and said nothing at all when it did not, so a reader could not tell an unnamed feature from a truncated sentence. 714 of the 3,047 nearest substations in this cut carry no name tag, and the gap reaches the top of the network: 34 of the 251 mapped 400 kV sites the fleet can reach are unnamed. The hover now says the layer has no name for it, and no name is inferred.
modification_note: One line of the SUB chip’s hover text, plus one sentence that appears only when the nearest substation is unnamed. No payload, no new asset, no render-time network call, and no change to the distance, the voltage, the caveats or any named row. Nothing is written into the name field: it stays empty and is described as empty.

app.label: an unnamed substation says so, and no name is invented for it

registry_entry.mutates_existing_dashboard: one line of the SUB chip hover, and one conditional line beneath it
registry_entry.rule: An empty field is described, never filled. Where the mapped layer carries no name for a feature, the surface says the layer carries no name for it and leaves the field empty. No recogniser, model or heuristic may write into a field a reader trusts and cannot check — the local settlement recogniser on this estate runs at 98.3% precision and its one failure was Rampton -> Rampson, which is plausible, wrong and uncheckable. Dropping the clause silently is the same failure in the other direction: it hides the gap instead of inventing over it.
registry_entry.found_by: Counted on releases/202609032251-pipelinenews on 2026-09-04 from the release’s own shipped payloads. In data/202608311858-substation-33kv.json, 2,333 of the 3,047 entries carry an `n` field and 714 do not. Taking every substation named in data/202608311610-grid-proximity.json — each row’s nearest plus its substations_nearby, deduplicated on coordinate — gives 4,737 distinct mapped substations, of which 1,154 (24.4%) have no name and 2,156 no operator. By voltage: 400 kV 34 unnamed of 251, 275 kV 28 of 226, 132 kV 185 of 1,178, 66 kV 28 of 282, 33 kV 912 of 3,451. The reader-facing effect was first seen from the other end, on the live Atlas card for REPD 155 (Markinch Biomass CHP), which answered “Nearest 400 kV substation: Unnamed substation · 28.82 km straight”; Pipeline News had the same gap and showed it as silence instead.
registry_entry.upstream: OpenStreetMap via the pinned Ventus voltage layers, ODbL-1.0, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors — the name tag is the layer’s, and its absence is the layer’s too.
